speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
text: asked the Minister for Transport (a) whether the next-generation ERP system allows for developers to create third-party applications; (b) whether the design of the on-board unit (OBU) be further streamlined for motorcyclists; and (c) whether the majority of the OBU's functions can be replaced by a smartphone in the future.

speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat
text: asked the Minister for Transport (a) whether the next-generation electronic road pricing (ERP) system is an open-source app-based device; (b) how will LTA allocate slots for installation of on-board units (OBU) to minimise queueing; (c) whether there is any replacement cost should the OBU get faulty after usage; and (d) in light of safety concerns about how the OBU's screen may be distracting to drivers, whether there can be an option to dim or turn off the display.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: asked the Minister for Transport (a) whether LTA will reduce the size and improve the design of the on-board units (OBUs) for all classes of vehicles for the next-generation ERP system to ensure safe use, avoid distraction to motorists and better interfacing with the vehicular dashboards and systems; and (b) whether LTA will assure Singaporeans that the price of the OBUs will be kept low and affordable.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The first question is why not process ERP payments using our smartphones?

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: After all, we use it to pay all kinds of transactions, including charges at HDB and URA carparks.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Technically, while this can be done, there will be many security and operational issues.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Hence, to better protect the system which contains the data of all motorists, we adopted the OBUs.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Motorists need to remember to bring their smartphones, ensure it is sufficiently charged, is connected to the cellular network and the ERP payment app is launched throughout the journey.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The second question is about the design of the OBU.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: So, if you compare, the OBU for motorcycles is only slightly larger than the current IU.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The dimensions: for the current OBU is 14 cm x 8 cm x 5 cm versus the current IU which is 13 cm x 8 cm x 4 cm; so 1 cm difference.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: But I concede it may look a little bulky because of the larger screen – but it is actually good for people like me.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: As for the OBUs for other vehicles, unlike for motorcycles, the processing unit will be installed below the dashboard and separated from the display unit on the screen.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: So, this is the processing unit but it is not going to be on your windscreen.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: It is actually going to be below the dashboard and it depends on the vehicle model where it will be put, but it will be out of sight.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: This is the processing unit and you can see that it has got ventilation, because it is actually a little CPU.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The processing unit is separated from the display screen and the antenna – this is necessary because the OBU uses Global Navigation Satellite Technology and is, like I said, really a little computer.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: There will be safety and reliability issues to leave the processing unit on the dashboard when vehicles with enclosed spaces are parked under the hot sun, similar to how we will not expose our smartphones that same way.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The OBU display unit will be mounted on the windscreen, and, actually, it is only slightly larger than the current IU.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: So, if Members look at this, it is about 3 cm longer but thinner.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The current IU is 12 cm x 8 cm x 3 cm versus the OBU's display screen which is 15 cm x 8 cm x 2 cm.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We are currently consulting the workshops and authorised motor vehicle agents on how best to install this display unit.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The antenna is actually very small, so it will be on the windscreen, where your current IU is.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: But we are looking at how to best install the OBU so that the display unit can be installed in cars such that the blockage of the windscreen is minimal.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Actually, this thing can be folded in, so that you will not see it if you do not want to see it.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: They are looking at how to do this better.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: As to what information to show on the display unit, indeed, we will look at how to make sure that whatever information is shown and the way it is shown, it will not be distracting and it will not affect safety.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: LTA intends to present a few options to gather public feedback.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: For example, the display can be kept black most of the time, and only display ERP charges paid when a transaction is effected.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: As a possible future upgrade, LTA is also studying whether information from the OBU can be pushed to our smartphones, then the smartphones can be used as the display screen instead.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Ms He Ting Ru1 has asked a question for the next Sitting on whether public consultation was done on the design – and we thought it is better we answer the question today.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Where possible, our practice is to consult the public, but in this case, LTA faces some practical constraints.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: This is a first-of-a-kind project – there is no similar system anywhere else in the world.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Several designs were submitted, and LTA has to select the best from the point of view of performance, design and value-for-money.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: But after awarding the tender, LTA is contractually bound.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: It could have specified that the winning tenderer has to conduct a major public consultation exercise and make significant changes to the design to take in public feedback, but that will add significant uncertainty which will delay the project and push up the tender prices.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
text: I have two supplementary questions for Senior Minister of State Khor.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
text: The first one is, if the concern is around the data protection, because today, under the OneMotoring.sg, all the details about every driver's particulars as well as the vehicle particulars are already available.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
text: Can we consider using the legal framework or data protection framework so that there is no concern in terms of information leakage.

speaker: Miss Cheryl Chan Wei Ling (East Coast)
text: The second supplementary question that I have is, because eventually there is a consideration, as Senior Minister of State had pointed out, to push this into the smartphone app, can we bring forward this implementation to make sure that we do not have to put on an additional gadgets on the dashboard or any part of the car frames.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: I want to thank the Member for the two supplementary questions.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The OBU interfaces, or speaks directly, to the backend ERP system and is able to access this.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We do not allow third-party apps or mobile phones to do the core charging function because there may be a compromise on the data – leakage, as well as the fact that there could be hacking, spoofing of the location and you can have fraudulent charging.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: For a system like that, you would want to maintain confidence in the system for our motorists as well as the fact that motorists must be confident that the vehicles' specific data will not be leaked.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: That is the reason why this is done.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: With regards to the second question about whether we can actually bring forward the timeline to look into whether we can allow data to be pushed one way, from the OBU to mobile phone and therefore, allow the mobile phone to replace the OBU display screen.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: What we want to do is to ensure a smooth implementation of the next-generation ERP system.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The current ERP system is already more than 20 years old, it is reaching its end of its operational life and, in fact, is increasingly difficult and actually very expensive to maintain.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Some of the parts are not going to be manufactured anymore.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: So, what we want, is to ensure a smooth installation of the nexgen ERP.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: To do this, the display unit will be a standard issue.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: We also need time to work with the contractors and the consultants to come up with the programme to be able to push OBU's specific data to the mobile app.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: And we will do it to the mobile phone third-party apps via bluetooth.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: What it means is that, motorists also have to give specific permissions for this to be done, they can then opt to use this mobile phone as the display screen.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: My first question is about the upcoming industry consultations that the LTA has planned, I would like to ask, what is the scope of this consultation and if the LTA is still open to doing a public consultation on the design of the onboard unit – perhaps for future considerations.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Like my fellow colleague, Miss Cheryl Chan have said, a lot of vehicles today already have display panels in the vehicle, can we then find a way to connect the OBU with the display that is already in existence in the vehicle.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: The second question I have pertains to the costs of embarking on a re-design of the OBU.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: In June 2019, when there was an online incident of a supposed design leak, LTA then had responded to state that the pictures were just illustrations used for an earlier study back in 2016.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: On 17 June last year, LTA stated through a Facebook post that the agency was still testing the equipment for the new ERP system, which has not been finalised.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: However, we also understand from Senior Minister of State's reply today that the LTA is contractually bound to the current OBU design after the tender award and any design changes would have cost implication.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
text: Therefore, I would like to ask the Senior Minister of State, what is the cost of re-designing the OBU at this current stage of the ERP contract and whether it would be more cost-effective to streamline the design now rather than embark on a redesign in the future.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: I want to thank the Member for his questions.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: I think it is useful to clarify these.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: So, this is what we are doing, we need time to work this out with the workshops, as well as the authorised motor vehicle agent, simply because there are so many different designs, make or models of motor vehicles.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: So, once we have done this, we will share more details on our public consultation with respect to the installation of the display unit.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: But having said that, we are open to taking feedback from the public, which we have done and we are going to do.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: One of the things we will do, is with regards to the Graphical User Interface or GUI, what to put on the display screen.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: LTA, taking into account public feedback, will come up with a few options.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Then, we will go out to do a public consultation again, to determine, you know, what are the important information to display with regards to driver safety, distractions and so on and so forth.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: In addition, we will see, as much feedback as possible, we will take into account within the bounds of our contractual obligations as well as the fact that you have to consider for instance, impact on the project timeline, technical viability is another other one, and of course safety requirements.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: So, the other one which we are doing and which we have taken feedback on, is of course with regard to the use of the mobile phone as a display screen.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: So, this is something that we are studying and we are looking to push this out.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: The Member Miss Cheryl Chan had asked if we do it as early as possible.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: For new car owners, they can actually opt for that, in future.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: That was four years ago, technology moves very quickly these days.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: So, I am just wondering what were the tender specifications that basically resulted in us being bound by the design that we committed to four years ago, rather than allowing for flexibility to update that as and when we went along?

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: And whether we will consider this in future tenders and future calls for tender to allow us to have greater flexibility given that technology moves really quickly?

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: And that, we do not inadvertently as in this case, end up incurring costs if we need to change the design as and when with public consultation and when technology moves along.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: I do not have the details of the contract, obviously, but I would think that, as with all contracts, there will always be certain specifications that have to be put out.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Otherwise, people cannot tender and you need to give contractors or tenderers some amount of certainty.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: But within those limits, I am pretty sure and I understand that there is room for some consultation.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: As the Member said it was in 2016 that the contract was awarded, it was early 2016.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: Within that time frame, we had consulted and the contractors themselves have also done some internal consultations as well as even engage, for instance, NTU, to do a study, a human factor study on the GUI features – what to display and so on.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: I understand that they even had a driver trial experiments to look at the safety of the GUI features.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: So, indeed, we are mindful that we have to take into account technology improvements and advancements which the contractors would have to do it.

speaker: Dr Amy Khor Lean Suan
text: But understanding that this is a very, very significant and large project, I think Members will also appreciate why the timeline is actually stretched.
